title: Proposal to Review Decision for "Dear You" Film to be Dubbed in Mandarin for General Commercial Release
what_it_is: Proposal to Review Decision for "Dear You" Film to be Dubbed in Mandarin for General Commercial Release

sections.label: Dear You Teochew screenings approved
sections.summary: IMDA approved 272 Teochew screenings of Dear You and may approve more, with scope to review dialect guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For the film "Dear You", IMDA has approved a total of 272 screenings of the Teochew version and is prepared to approve additional screenings should the film distributor request them in response to audience demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Beyond these implementation changes, several Members have called for the guidelines themselves to be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We recognise that the circumstances have changed since the guidelines were first introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: There is, therefore, scope to consider how we can expand the space for dialects, while continuing to uphold the importance of Mandarin.

sections.label: Cinema dialect film screenings
sections.summary: Cinemas may be allowed more dialect-language film screenings, comparing Parasite, How to Make Millions, and Dear You's versions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For cinemas, we are prepared to allow more screenings of dialect-language films, so as to provide audiences with greater access to such content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Locally, "Parasite" screened close to 12,000 sessions. "How to Make Millions before Grandma Dies" around 5,000. "Dear You", in Mandarin, 2,570; while its Teochew version, the original, a mere 126 public screenings as of early-July.

sections.label: Flexibility for Teochew screenings
sections.summary: The number cited was updated to 272, and flexibility will continue if the distributor sees audience demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The Member talked about screening of the original Teochew dialect of the film being popular.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We have said that we will provide flexibility and we will continue to provide flexibility, in fact, the number that the Member cited has been updated in my reply, I said, 272, if the Member listened carefully just now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The film distributor knows that we will continue to provide flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: So, in practice, if the film distributor feels that audience demand is there for the Teochew original film, we will provide flexibility.

sections.label: Expanding dialect movie access
sections.summary: The language environment has changed and access to dialect movies may be expanded during the review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Having said that, as I have explained in my reply, we appreciate that the language environment has changed and we are prepared to see how we can expand access to dialect movies as we undertake our review.

sections.label: NAC Chinese opera support
sections.summary: NAC supported Tan Wei Tian's studies and funded 10 opera productions spanning Hokkien, Teochew, Cantonese and Hainanese.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: For example, NAC supported Tan Wei Tian, a young Chinese Opera artist, who has performed with Nam Hwa Opera from a young age, to pursue a Bachelor’s in Chinese Opera Performing at the Shanghai Theatre Academy in China in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Last year, NAC and Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre co-presented the inaugural Chinese Opera Festival, featuring five local troupes performing across different opera styles.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: In 2025 alone, NAC funded 10 productions, spanning Hokkien, Teochew, Cantonese and Hainanese opera.

sections.label: Preserving dialect cultures feedback
sections.summary: MCCY and MDDI are open to ideas on preserving dialect cultures while upholding Mandarin, and will consider next steps.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Neo
sentences.text: As I explained earlier, MCCY and MDDI are open to ideas about how can we preserve dialect cultures while upholding the importance of Mandarin, and we will continue to take in all the feedback and consider carefully the appropriate next steps on how to do this well.

sections.label: Review of dialect film classification
sections.summary: The film classification framework is being reviewed regarding the use of dialect in films.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We welcome it as part of a conversation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And as part of this conversation, we are reviewing our current film classification framework with respect to the use of dialect in films.

sections.label: Additional screenings approved for film distributor
sections.summary: Another 100 screenings were approved today, bringing the total to 272, with more flexibility possible if demand grows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The film distributor knows that we are giving him flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I had earlier mentioned, we approved another 100 screenings today, that brings up the number of screenings to 272.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: If there is more demand, we will discuss it with the film distributor and see how we can provide additional flexibility.

sections.label: IMDA policy reflection question
sections.summary: A question asks how this is reflected in IMDA's policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: If so, how is this reflected in IMDA's policy?

sections.label: Government reviews dialect film approach
sections.summary: The Government has reviewed its approach to dialect films as Singapore's linguistic landscape evolved, and will consider further relaxing restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In fact, as Singapore's linguistic landscape has evolved, the Government has from time to time reviewed its approach to dialect films, adjusting to meet demand and allowing for greater dialect content in films where appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will continue to listen to public feedback and give serious consideration to whether restrictions can be further relaxed, so as to increase the number of screenings of dialect films and give local audiences more opportunities to access and appreciate them.

sections.label: More Teochew screenings, Mandarin objective
sections.summary: More Teochew dialect film screenings can be allowed if demand grows, while promoting the speaking of Mandarin remains the objective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: If demand grows, we can allow more screenings of Teochew dialect films.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But what is equally important is that we do not lose sight of our original objective – and that objective is to promote the speaking of Mandarin.

sections.label: Radio station for dialect songs
sections.summary: A suggestion is made to designate one of six radio stations to play olden days songs, about 50% Mandarin and 50% dialects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The problem, however, is that they are currently unable to listen to dialect songs due to existing restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wonder whether we might consider designating one of our six radio stations to play songs from the olden days – perhaps with around 50% in Mandarin and the remaining 50% in dialects.

sections.label: Mandarin, dialect news, film policy
sections.summary: Television and radio must keep Mandarin mainstream, dialect news serves seniors, and the film policy will be reviewed after "Dear You" was well received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Our television and radio stations should not lose sight of their original purpose and must keep Mandarin as the mainstream language.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Similarly, at 10.30 am, 11.30 am and 12.30 pm, dialect news broadcasts are available on a radio station to cater to the needs of our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: More importantly, we have taken note of the warm reception that "Dear You" has received from our people, and we will look into this film policy further.
